assertions.subject: delirium
assertions.quote: Commonly, among dying patients, delirium can be caused by side effects of treatments, including radiation for brain metastases, and medications, including opioids, glucocorticoids, anticholinergic drugs, antihistamines, antiemetics, benzodiazepines, and chemotherapeutic agents.

assertions.quote: In the weeks or months before death, delirium is uncommon, although it may be significantly under-diagnosed.

assertions.quote: Up to 85% of patients dying from cancer may experience terminal delirium.

assertions.subject: dementia
assertions.quote: In contrast to dementia, delirium has an acute onset, is characterized by fluctuating consciousness and inattention, and is reversible, although reversibility may be more theoretical than real for patients near death.
